title: Writing the Focus string pieces for Stan Getz
summary: He wrote bare string parts that let Getz find his way.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Why it took the shape it did I can't ascribe to anything else except I wanted to do something for strings. I lost my fear of it because they would never let me handle these things. I wasn't a string man. They used to label you; they still do. If you're a jazz man you can't be something else. You know how it is.

I lost my fear of it through working on shows and working with Bobby Doland on certain TV scores. Then it gave me a chance--how to make it work for Stan was a big problem and it took me a long time to figure that one out, because I didn't
want to write goose eggs. I didn't want to write the smathered rhythm section because to me that wouldn't have been any fun. There's nothing wrong with it, but I didn't want to do that.

I figured the only way I could do it was to write a bare bones affair that had--that could stand by itself somehow so that I could also make my relationship and let Stan find his way through this stuff. Sometimes there was a melody there, sometimes there wasn't.
Did you write parts for him?
Yes. Mostly I wrote a melody where there was a melody. I would only do what they call a condensed set, so he could see what the other people were doing, and he went his own way.
On this one I didn't do that, (inaudible); how could he know where to be, so I wrote it out, and play it as you please.
